report:
### Evidence Summary on Ivermectin and COVID-19

Based on high-quality scientific evidence, **ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19 patients**.

While early laboratory (in vitro) research showed that high doses of ivermectin could inhibit viral replication, rigorous human clinical trials have consistently demonstrated no significant clinical benefit:

1. **Large Clinical Trials:** Large, double-blind randomized controlled trials (RCTs)—such as the TOGETHER trial—found that ivermectin did not significantly reduce hospital admissions, emergency care visits, or mortality compared to placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
2. **Systematic Reviews:** Comprehensive systematic reviews evaluating pooled trial data concluded that high-certainty evidence shows ivermectin does not reduce COVID-19 mortality or improve clinical recovery outcomes (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361442829_Ivermectin_for_preventing_and_treating_COVID-19).
3. **Medical & Regulatory Consensus:** Major health authorities, including the U.S. FDA, NIH, World Health Organization (WHO), and Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), recommend against using ivermectin to treat or prevent COVID-19 outside of clinical trials (https://www.drugs.com/ivermectin.html, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic).

Initial claims suggesting a significant reduction in mortality were primarily based on small, unblinded, or observational studies with high risks of bias or methodological flaws. When subjected to rigorous trial designs, ivermectin demonstrates no mortality benefit against COVID-19.
